blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, with `if (obj instanceof Square square) { ... } else { ... }`, where can code use `square`?

options.text: In both blocks, as the variable is declared in the condition
options.says: The page says square is not accessible in the else block.

options.text: In the if block only, where the match is known to hold
options.says: The page says the pattern variable is in scope only where the match succeeded: here, the if block.

options.text: Anywhere after the if, as far as the end of the method
options.says: The page says square is not accessible after the if statement in this example.

questions.stem: Per this page, what may code do with a pattern variable such as `s` in `obj instanceof String s`?

options.text: Assign it a new value, unless the pattern marks it final
options.says: The page says a pattern variable is not implicitly final and can be reassigned unless declared final.

options.text: Read it, but never assign it, as it is implicitly final
options.says: The page says the pattern variable is not implicitly final.

options.text: Use it as a String only after casting it once more
options.says: The page says pattern matching eliminates the need for explicit casting after the instanceof check.

concepts: A pattern variable is not implicitly final: it can be reassigned unless declared final.
A pattern variable is in scope only where the match is certain, not in the else block or after the if.
